# Database and entitlement foundation

Billing/admin storage and server-only entitlement helpers now feed actions,
workers, quota reporting, preferences and UI. The sending control is enforced at
campaign creation, dispatch and both delivery checks. Paid gating remains off by
default; this implementation does not enable it.

Existing and future users default to Free, subscription status NONE, non-admin
and unsuspended. No subscriptions, overrides, grandfathering, activity or
billing dates are inferred. Free template eligibility uses the owned, active
selection or the oldest active template, breaking ties by ID. Legacy bounce storage stays unchanged. Recipient suppression storage was subsequently
removed by 20261016020000_remove_recipient_suppression. IDs remain application-generated UUID strings
in PostgreSQL TEXT columns; dates remain TIMESTAMP(3).

## Helper contract

Effective access uses [start, end) boundaries, including subscriptions scheduled
to cancel at period end. Precedence: deletion/suspension, active override,
grandfathering, verified subscription projection, Free. Free overrides take
precedence over grandfathering. PAST_DUE requires an explicit valid grace
deadline. Admin status grants no access or bypass.

requireEntitlement is an internal helper, not a Server Action. Entry points must
authenticate and obtain userId from the session; service jobs must verify their
service boundary. Reads use an explicit token-free selection, without caching.
An optional transaction keeps reads within the caller's transaction; callers
remain responsible for locks and resource-specific checks. Missing controls
deny access; database errors propagate.

Template checks grant baseline access only. Counts, selected-template ownership,
and active-template policy are enforced by template-policy under the User lock.
Sending checks do not reserve quota or replace Gmail preflight/OAuth ciphertext validation.

The client DTO explicitly allowlists fields and contains configured limits,
while quota snapshots supply remaining usage and reset timestamps. The workspace
provider refreshes both together; the flag-off quota API retains its legacy
shape. Basic tracking means Sent/Failed;
manual reply marking is a separate entitlement. Unlimited saved templates
serialize as null.

Gating off preserves legacy CSV, reminder and manual reply access. Custom-role caps apply independently of the gating switch.
Premium themes and preview highlight color customization also apply independently of the gating switch. Free previews use Cyan without overwriting a saved Premium color preference.
Priority support is new and still requires Paid. Account export/deletion,
cancellation and ordinary support remain outside paid
feature gates.

addContactToShortlist, saveContact and campaign resends use manualRepeatSend,
which is included in both Free and Premium. addToShortlist also requires
historyShortlist: the History shortcut is Premium-only when paid gating is enabled.
Free users can re-enter and save contact details to restore a repeat recipient
automatically; Premium users can use the History + shortcut. Durable delivery
receipts remain evidence after history removal. Re-saving updates or restores the
same contact and prepares a follow-up without sending. Compose requires individual
selection of previously emailed recipients; Select all skips them. Each repeat
email counts toward daily, monthly and campaign limits. checkContactEmail remains
available to show the same non-blocking warning on both plans.
Both markReplied and undoReply require Paid when gating is enabled. Existing reply
history remains readable and exportable. Reminder Off remains available to everyone.
Free includes 1 custom role; Premium includes up to 20. Saved role shortcuts have a separate limit of 5 on Free and 20 on Premium. Existing shortcuts survive a downgrade and may be retained or removed, while additions above the current plan limit are blocked. Count distinct normalized titles across shortcuts and active contacts. Existing custom titles remain usable even over the cap; only new titles are blocked. Replacements may use capacity freed by the same save. Compose overrides share remaining capacity within a batch without persisting titles. Approved queued role snapshots remain eligible after downgrade. Free users may switch their single eligible template; retained
extras remain viewable, exportable and archivable. Invalid campaigns lose their
READY remainder on downgrade, with only definitely unsubmitted capacity released.
Deleting completed history while a campaign is active hides and redacts message
content but retains original size/role evidence until the campaign is terminal,
so history deletion cannot make an invalid queued remainder eligible.

No integration is planned here with automatic reply stubs, suppression,
bounce marking or automatic follow-up workers. Usage models, follow-up
sequences, EntitlementGrant, sending-pause/cleanup fields, Gmail-read fields,
rollout/checkout flags and automatic tracking flags are excluded.

## Database invariants and deployment

SQL CHECK constraints are maintained in the migration; do not replace them
with db push. Related billing/override/suspension fields must be updated
atomically. Nullable periods support pending/failed records. Checkout and
webhook state fields remain open strings for future worker design.

SystemControl has at most one row with key global, seeded by the migration.
Missing-row handling denies access. Prisma generates UUIDs and updatedAt;
raw SQL writers supply IDs and updatedAt (the singleton seed uses PostgreSQL
gen_random_uuid). Webhooks and controls are service-owned. Provider IDs are
external strings.

Future verified billing handlers must maintain User projection and subscription
history transactionally. JSON writers must allowlist billing/audit metadata:
database JSON-object checks cannot enforce privacy. Audit snapshots survive
user deletion. Revisit billing/checkout cascade and financial retention policy
before billing launches.

Apply the additive migration before deploying code that queries the new fields;
generate Prisma Client explicitly. ALTER TABLE and ordinary index creation
acquire locks; schedule deployment with representative data in mind.

Verification uses disposable local databases ending in _test. New database tests
use unique schemas, clean them in finally/teardown (including setup failure),
and reject remote/non-test targets before writes. Run the entire database suite
serially using npm run test:db -- --no-file-parallelism. PostgreSQL stays in
Docker; tools and Next.js run on the host. Do not migrate the application
database as part of this verification.

For rollback, revert application code and leave additive schema and singleton
in place. The old application ignores them. Do not edit applied migrations,
reset the database or drop billing/audit evidence. Transactional migration
failure rolls back; correct before retry. Any schema removal needs a separate
reviewed migration.

## Verification

`npm run test:usage:db -- --e2e` applies existing migrations to a fresh,
loopback-only PostgreSQL container, runs database checks, then the feature-gate,
app, landing and policy browser suites before cleanup. The test application runs
on the host in `.next-e2e`, separately from the normal development server.
`--e2e-only --browser=feature-gates` repeats selected browser coverage with a new
disposable database. Neither mode uses the application database.
